entries.title: De Reus van Bickerseiland
entries.hook: A wooden Roman soldier taken to Alicante in 1972, traced by islanders to Canada, home again in 2009.

entries.title: The oldest wild fig of Amsterdam, Drieharingenbrug
entries.hook: Nobody planted it: a fig seeded itself into the quay wall around 1990 and now bears fruit.

entries.title: Haarlemmer Houttuinen: the motorway that stopped at a bridge
entries.reason: replacement plan of the bridge to check
entries.hook: A car bridge built for a motorway that never came, painted by one of Europe's first women graffiti writers.

entries.title: "De walvis" and the poem on the quay, Hollandse Tuin
entries.hook: A granite fountain-sculpture islanders call the whale, and a neighbour's poem cut into the quay wall.

entries.title: Tuin Bickersgracht Noordkop and De Dierencapel
entries.reason: pin approximate; tree-felling plan outcome unknown
entries.hook: A neighbour-kept garden reserve with bird islands at the island's tip, beside the children's farm saved in 2006.

entries.title: Kunstroute Nieuwe Houttuinen
entries.hook: One resident turned "a road from nowhere to nowhere" into an art route: Jonas and the whale, eye-twisting underpasses.

entries.title: Jacob van Lennep and the first water tap
entries.hook: A steel-and-glass statue twelve years after its fountain fell through, where the city's first dune water was sold.

entries.title: Door wind bewogen beweging (Wicher Meursing)
entries.hook: Friends built the designer's wind sculpture from his model after his death; it swings or stands dead still.

entries.title: De Roode Bioscoop, the anarchists' cinema
entries.reason: outcome of the 2024 name case unknown (Under threat)
entries.hook: An anarchist's 1913 cinema "to spread red ideas", now a volunteer stage fighting its landlord over the name.

entries.title: Prinseneiland: the last walwindas, the Palmentuin and Mandela's garden
entries.reason: winch spot and garden access to check; mural maker unknown
entries.hook: The city's last shore-winch cover for tar barrels, a neighbour-made garden, and a mural of Mandela's prison garden.

entries.title: De Aardige Amsterdammer, Droogbak
entries.hook: An outstretched hand for the volunteers who help the homeless; stolen on King's Day 2015, remade.

entries.title: Zandhoek: the Oranjeboom and Stadsherstel's first house
entries.reason: which tree needs a site check; single source for the tree
entries.hook: Wilhelmina's 1898 lime behind its small fence, and De Keijser, the first house Stadsherstel restored (1959).

entries.title: De Mof and the widow called Sluys, Haarlemmerdijk 109
entries.reason: shop (borderline); the name is a wartime slur, careful copy
entries.hook: Neighbours nicknamed a German workwear seller "de mof" in 1885; the SLUYS stone above names a widow, not a town.

entries.title: Vinkenstraat, a wall that makes you see suns
entries.hook: Stare at Roland Schimmel's black circles and coloured after-images appear; a folded-steel square a few steps on.

entries.title: Wubboboom, Haarlemmerplein
entries.reason: Okay; or a Look for line in Willem Drees's birthplace (same square)
entries.hook: An elm for astronaut Wubbo Ockels with benches quoting "we are all astronauts of Spaceship Earth".

entries.title: De Oude Amsterdammer, Korte Prinsengracht 5
entries.hook: A corner house whose shopfront with two doors still shows the old bar.

entries.title: Stones that came home, Bickersgracht 14 and 22
entries.hook: A vanished 1664 gable stone turned up in a dentist's wall in Moordrecht and was bricked back in.

entries.title: Toon Ylandplantsoen, "ons klein Keukenhof"
entries.hook: An orphaned strip turned neighbours' garden, named in 2016 behind its gardener's back after him.

entries.title: Het Groene Hoofd aan het IJ
entries.reason: Okay; single source; or a Look for line in Rederij Goedkoop
entries.hook: Two residents turned a tug firm's concrete mooring platform into planters and benches, shovelling the grit themselves.

entries.title: Gables that swim: Abraham Zeeman's sea fish and De Hond's dolphins
entries.hook: A man named Seaman had his gable claws carved as sea fish around 1715.

enrich.draft: Posthoorn church and its Catholic island
enrich.add: the predecessor hidden church in the post-coach house De Posthoorn, Prinsengracht 7 (c. 1687), posthorn still in the front

enrich.add: line: the rail yard's wild flora and the lost IJ view of the Westerdokseiland
Look for: 't Bronzen vingertje for street manager Nel de Jager (2021, stolen, crowdfunded back 2023)

enrich.add: Look for: the hoisting wheel inside (café)
